title: Trait Objects and Dynamic Dispatch
goal: Understand why dynamic dispatch requires indirection behind pointers.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Morning: Trait Objects

sections.text: In languages like Java or Go, all interface references use dynamic dispatch automatically. Rust makes dynamic dispatch explicit with the `dyn` keyword.

sections.caption: A trait defines shared behavior without specifying a concrete type.

sections.text: A raw `dyn Speaker` type has no fixed size at compile time. Rust requires types in variables and function arguments to have a known size.

sections.code:
// Error E0277: dyn Speaker unsized
// fn announce(s: dyn Speaker) { ... }
sections.caption: Unsized trait objects cannot be passed directly by value.

sections.text: To use dynamic dispatch, put `dyn Trait` behind a pointer such as `&dyn Speaker` or `Box<dyn Speaker>`.

sections.caption: &dyn Speaker is a fat pointer holding a data pointer and a vtable pointer.

sections.text: Monomorphization creates separate functions for every generic type. Dynamic dispatch uses one function and looks up methods in a vtable at runtime.

explanation: Understand why dynamic dispatch requires indirection behind pointers.
